item.title: Bhikkhus, just as a bitter gourd mixed with poison. Then a person comes who wants to live, does not want to die, wants happiness, and…
item.description:
Bhikkhus, just as a bitter gourd mixed with poison. Then a person comes who wants to live, does not want to die, wants happiness, and loathes suffering. Someone says to him: 'Friend, this bitter gourd is mixed with poison. If you wish, eat it. While eating, you will not enjoy its color, smell, or taste. After eating, you may die or suffer deadly pain.' He might eat it without reflection, without giving it up. While eating, he does not enjoy its color, smell, or taste. After eating, he dies or suffers deadly pain. Bhikkhus, I say that this course of practice is like that simile — that is, a course of practice that is painful in the present and also has a painful result in the future.

From: Majjhima Nikāya 46 – Mahādhammasamādānasutta

item.title: Thinking of their own good, They rob and harm others, When others rob and harm them, The robber becomes the robbed. The fool thinks thus,…
item.description:
Thinking of their own good,
They rob and harm others,
When others rob and harm them,
The robber becomes the robbed.

The fool thinks thus,
When evil is not yet ripe,
When evil becomes ripe,
The fool experiences suffering.

Killing, one is killed,
Conquering, one is conquered,
Abusing, one is abused,
Harassing, one is harassed,
Thus action evolves,
The robber becomes the robbed.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 3.15

item.title: Vāseṭṭha, what do you think? Have you heard the elderly, senior brahmins, teachers and great teachers, talking together: Does Brahmā have sensual desire or not?…
item.description:
Vāseṭṭha, what do you think? Have you heard the elderly, senior brahmins, teachers and great teachers, talking together: Does Brahmā have sensual desire or not? — Master Gotama, he has no sensual desire. — Does he have hatred or not? — He has no hatred. — Does he have ill-will or not? — He has no ill-will. — Does he have defilement or not? — He has no defilement. — Does he have self-mastery or not? — He has self-mastery. — Vāseṭṭha, what do you think? Do the brahmins proficient in the three Vedas have sensual desire or not? — Master Gotama, they have sensual desire. — Do they have hatred or not? — They have hatred. — Do they have ill-will or not? — They have ill-will. — Do they have defilement or not? — They have defilement. — Do they have self-mastery or not? — They have no self-mastery. — Vāseṭṭha, you say that the brahmins proficient in the three Vedas have sensual desire, and Brahmā has no sensual desire. Can there be association and co-residence between the brahmins proficient in the three Vedas who have sensual desire and Brahmā who has no sensual desire? — Master Gotama, that is impossible. — Good, Vāseṭṭha. Then, Vāseṭṭha, that those brahmins proficient in the three Vedas, being full of sensual desire, after death, with the breakup of the body, should be reborn in companionship with Brahmā — that is impossible.

From: Dīgha Nikāya 13 – Tevijjasutta

item.title: - Venerable Kotthika, does the Tathāgata exist after death?... Does the Tathāgata neither exist nor does not exist after death?... When asked thus, the venerable…
item.description:
- Venerable Kotthika, does the Tathāgata exist after death?... Does the Tathāgata neither exist nor does not exist after death?... When asked thus, the venerable one answers: 'The Blessed One does not answer: "The Tathāgata exists after death... The Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death."' For what reason, venerable sir, for what condition does the Blessed One not answer that question?" - "Friend, for one who has lust for form, who delights in form, who rejoices in form, who does not truly know and see the cessation of form, that person may have the view: 'The Tathāgata exists after death... The Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death.' Friend, for one who has lust for feeling... for perception... for formations... Friend, for one who has lust for consciousness, who delights in consciousness, who rejoices in consciousness, who does not truly know and see the cessation of consciousness, that person may have the view: 'The Tathāgata exists after death... The Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death.' Friend, this is the cause, this is the condition, this is the reason why the Blessed One does not answer that question.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 44.6

item.title: 'Empty is the world, empty is the world,' Venerable Sir, is said. To what extent, Venerable Sir, is the world called empty?" - "Because, Ānanda,…
item.description:
'Empty is the world, empty is the world,' Venerable Sir, is said. To what extent, Venerable Sir, is the world called empty?" - "Because, Ānanda, the world is empty of self and of anything belonging to self, therefore the world is called empty. And what, Ānanda, is empty of self and of anything belonging to self? The eye, Ānanda, is empty of self and of anything belonging to self. Forms are empty of self and of anything belonging to self. Eye-consciousness is empty of self and of anything belonging to self. Eye-contact is empty ... Whatever feeling arises dependent on eye-contact ... that feeling is empty of self and of anything belonging to self. ... The ear ... The nose ... The tongue ... The body ... The mind is empty of self and of anything belonging to self. Mind-objects ... Mind-consciousness ... Mind-contact ... Whatever feeling arises dependent on mind-contact ... that feeling is empty of self and of anything belonging to self. And because it is empty of self and of anything belonging to self, Ānanda, the world is called empty.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 35.85

item.title: Bhikkhus, these three things lead to the decline of a learner bhikkhu. What three? Here, bhikkhus, a learner bhikkhu delights in work, takes pleasure in…
item.description:
Bhikkhus, these three things lead to the decline of a learner bhikkhu. What three? Here, bhikkhus, a learner bhikkhu delights in work, takes pleasure in work, is devoted to delight in work; delights in talking, takes pleasure in talking, is devoted to delight in talking; delights in sleeping, takes pleasure in sleeping, is devoted to delight in sleeping.

A bhikkhu who delights in work,
Delights in talking,
Delights in sleeping,
Is restless and agitated.
Such a bhikkhu cannot attain
Supreme enlightenment.

Therefore, let him have few duties,
Little sleep, no restlessness,
Such a bhikkhu can attain
Supreme enlightenment.

From: Itivuttaka 79

item.title: Possessing these five qualities, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is fit to live separate from the Saṅgha. What five? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is content with such…
item.description:
Possessing these five qualities, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is fit to live separate from the Saṅgha. What five? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is content with such robes as he receives here and there; is content with such almsfood as he receives here and there; is content with such lodgings as he receives here and there; is content with such medicinal requisites as he receives here and there; and he dwells with many thoughts of renunciation. Possessing these five qualities, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is fit to live separate from the Saṅgha.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 5.127

item.title: Here, friends, a person has defilements but does not truly understand: 'There are defilements within me.' For such a person, this can be expected: 'He…
item.description:
Here, friends, a person has defilements but does not truly understand: 'There are defilements within me.' For such a person, this can be expected: 'He will not arouse desire, will not make effort, will not arouse energy to abandon those defilements. He will die while still having greed, still having hatred, still having delusion, still having defilements, still having a defiled mind.' Friends, just as a bronze bowl, brought from the market or from the smithy, covered with dust and grime, and its owner does not use it, does not clean it, and throws it into a dusty place. Friends, after a time, that bowl becomes even more defiled, even dustier.

From: Majjhima Nikāya 5 – Anaṅgaṇasutta

item.title: An Arahant bhikkhu, Who has done what had to be done, The taints destroyed, This body, his last body. Can he say: 'I speak'? Can…
item.description:
An Arahant bhikkhu,
Who has done what had to be done,
The taints destroyed,
This body, his last body.
Can he say:
'I speak'?
Can he say:
'They speak to me'?
( Blessed One ):
An Arahant bhikkhu,
Who has done what had to be done,
The taints destroyed,
This body, his last body.
He can say:
'I speak',
He can say:
'They speak to me'.
Skilfully knowing
Mere conventions in the world,
Using such conventions,
He would speak accordingly.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 1.25

item.title: ( Blessed One ): Thinking oneself equal, better, or worse, Conflict arises from that; One who is unmoved by these three, For them equal and…
item.description:
( Blessed One ):
Thinking oneself equal, better, or worse,
Conflict arises from that;
One who is unmoved by these three,
For them equal and better do not arise.

Give up reckoning,
Do not chase after vain thoughts,
Abandon all craving
For name-and-form in the world.
That one cuts the fetters,
Without worry, without craving.
Devas and humans,
In this world or the next,
In the deva realms,
Or in any abode,
Searching, they cannot find
The footprint of that one.

Throughout the world, do not do
Evil by body, speech, or mind.
Abandon all sensual desires,
Mindful, with clear comprehension,
Without torturing the body,
Vain and unbeneficial.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 1.20
